ai_patterns_removed: archaic scripture-register dialogue modernized throughout ("Kesava hath gone to the sons of Pritha", "he will surely stimulate the Pandavas", "wicked-souled wight", "beareth no good will", "casting off all sloth") into plain timeless speech with every point of Duryodhana's war-readiness speech kept

"like the great Indra surrounded by the Adityas" epic simile and the ally name-census (Kekayas/Vrishnis/car-warrior count) compressed into one plain sentence; the moonlit-ocean simile kept but shortened to its strongest images
heavy single-block opening (source-translation list style) broken into short story paragraphs starting close to the event
child_friendly_changes: opener establishes who the Pandavas are and why they are on the field (lost kingdom at a rigged game of dice, exile served, peace refused) so the story stands alone
Karna, Dussasana, and Sakuni introduced by relationship (dearest friend / brother / uncle who won the dice game) instead of bare names
Kuru capital named Hastinapura; Krishna's failed peace mission explained in one clause

ai_patterns_removed: mid-thought archaic opener ("How, O Kesava, could wicked Duryodhana say it?") replaced with a plain scene-setting opening

Krishna's long court-recap monologue — a near-verbatim repeat of DKS_0451's speech — compressed and modernized ("wicked-souled wight", "deceit supplieth the place of wisdom", "regardeth everything as already won", "obtain the fruition of that wish") without losing one point

Archaic laments modernized ("that great calamity overtaketh us of a set purpose", "whom we on no account can slay"); epic-title clutter (Janardana, Sankarshana, Devaki's son, Savyasachin) rendered as plain names
lecture-style closing summary replaced by a quiet image of the charioteer taking the reins
child_friendly_changes: first-sentence context names the quarrel (Pandavas vs their Kaurava cousins over their grandfathers' kingdom) so it reads without DKS_0451
Vidura, Bhishma, and Kunti identified by role (court counselor / old grandsire / the Pandavas' mother) as they appear
the attempted seizure of Krishna at the Kuru court stated plainly and kept
risk: Krishna's catalogue of Duryodhana's faults — deceit in place of wisdom, deafness to Bhishma/Vidura/Krishna, reliance on Karna, the order to seize Krishna, the silence of Bhishma and Drona with Vidura the sole voice against, Sakuni/Karna/Dussasana's bad counsel — preserved point by point in the compression. 'Devaki's son' rendered as plain 'Krishna' (same person).

ai_patterns_removed: the long recap of the previous story (army arraying, soldiers' joy, Yudhishthira's sigh with full quotation) that filled the first third of the story compressed to two narrative sentences — the lament belongs to DKS_0452 and now only echoes
archaic speech modernized ("seeketh", "I shall now repair to the tirtha of the Saraswati for ablutions", "behold with indifference") into plain speech
opening moved from recap to the story's own hero, Balarama, standing apart
child_friendly_changes: one context sentence identifies the two sides as two branches of one royal family (five sons of Pandu vs hundred sons of the blind king Dhritarashtra)
Balarama introduced as Krishna's elder brother, a warrior of the Vrishni clan
tirthas explained naturally as the Saraswati's holy bathing-fords where pilgrims wash and pray; the brothers' parting made explicit
risk: Balarama's core statement kept nearly word for word in meaning: "I cannot bear to face the world without Krishna on my side; whatever Krishna sets out to achieve, I follow" and "I cannot look on unmoved while the Kauravas are destroyed." The interpretive line "the only way to be true to both was to stand with neither" restates the file's own closing judgment and adds no new fact. Reflection rewritten to remove the "The story is a quiet acknowledgment that..." framing (house style s18); meaning unchanged.

ai_patterns_removed: theologically dense epithet catalogue (approx. 150 words of untranslated names: 'identical with Brahman', 'Swaha and Swadha', 'Saraswati and Savitri', 'Srutis', 'science of Brahma', 'Siddhas and Charanas') compressed to the essential names with the 'many names' frame kept
'Perhaps it was that last line that was heard' speculative flourish removed
register smoothed: 'O thou that art...' litany rhythm replaced with plain storytelling
child_friendly_changes: opening explains the cousins' quarrel (insult, exile, rigged dice game) in one sentence so it stands alone

every name kept is glossed in the same sentence: Durga the goddess, Kali/Mahakali, Kaitabha named a demon, Skanda glossed as the war-god, Nanda identified as the cowherd chief who raised Krishna, Asuras/Danavas rendered as demons, Vedas as the oldest sacred songs

Narayana glossed as 'the Lord whom men call Krishna'; the thunderbolt-wielder named as Indra, king of the gods; Nara and Narayana explained as the ancient seer-pair whose forms Arjuna and Krishna were said to take; Vyasa/Dwaipayana, Narada, Kanwa, and 'the blameless Rama' (Balarama, Krishna's brother) each identified
risk: The goddess's promise kept almost verbatim in meaning — 'within a short time you shall conquer your enemies'; 'you cannot be defeated... not even by Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt' — and the Sanjaya coda (hymn's protective powers, the Kauravas 'caught in the net of death', the sages' failed warnings, 'where righteousness is, there victory is') preserved in order. Hymn epithets were compressed, none given new attributes.

ai_patterns_removed: archaic dialogue modernized: 'O one who knows no deterioration' dropped, 'Behold, O Partha, these assembled Kurus' rendered 'Look, Arjuna — these Kurus, gathered before you', 'I wish not to slay these, though they slay me, not even for the sovereignty of the three worlds' kept in full meaning but plain register
crowded double name-list of Duryodhana's review trimmed while every named champion (both sides) is retained

'the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra' kept as Duryodhana's plain description; kinship catalogue rendered by relationship (grandfathers, grandsons, father-in-law, teachers, uncles, brothers-in-law) instead of epic lists
